strengths: The paper addresses a relevant problem with an identifiable audience in code representation learning and binary analysis. Aligning LLVM IR with source code and comments through frozen anchors and learned interpolation is a plausible, useful approach.

The reported results suggest benefits on several tasks: POJ-104 MAP increases from the strongest listed baseline's 39.99 to 43.78, function-name accuracy from 29.41 to 33.41, and summarization BLEU-4 from 32.43 to 34.36.

The evaluation covers four tasks and includes component ablations, a CodeT5 extension, and negative examples. Investigating how comment preparation affects training is particularly relevant to practitioners.
The diagrams and equations communicate the overall training strategy, and the manuscript provides a public archive link for implementation and data.
weaknesses: Necessary—resolve the POJ-104 evaluation protocol. Sections 2.3 and 4.2 describe supervised classification into 104 classes, but Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify disjoint sets of 64 training, 16 development, and 24 test labels. Ordinary classification does not explain prediction of unseen classes. If this is actually retrieval, specify the training objective, candidate pool, relevance definition, and MAP/MAR/MAF1 calculations. This ambiguity affects both the main results and nearly all ablations.

Necessary—align the binary-analysis claims with the evaluated inputs. The experiments use compiler-generated LLVM IR, and Figures 7–8 retain informative function, global, and type names. Such inputs are not trivially interchangeable with stripped native executables, as the introductory footnote suggests. Either restrict the claims to the evaluated IR setting or provide evidence using an explicit executable-to-IR pipeline with appropriate symbol handling.

Necessary—make the AnghaBench evaluation partition unambiguous. Section 3.2 says generation is evaluated on the validation set, whereas Section 4.3 says the test set is used. Explain how the pretraining holdout is partitioned for downstream training, model selection, and final evaluation, and describe overlap checks. Also state explicitly whether evaluation summaries are CodeT5-generated. These details determine what the generation results establish.

Necessary—separate interpolation effects from additional training. PCL and the interpolation-removal ablation receive 10 pretraining epochs, while the full model receives 30 or 70. Section 5.1 asserts convergence but supplies no supporting evidence. A matched-training comparison is needed for the causal attribution to interpolation, or that attribution should be narrowed. The current experiments also do not distinguish the contributions of scalar and feature-wise interpolation.

Necessary—qualify the comment-quality conclusion. Human-written comments yield 3.06 MAF1, versus 38.19 with generated comments, but removing comments yields 37.40. This establishes a striking sensitivity in the reported setup; it does not establish the proposed explanations involving verbosity, implementation detail, and writing style. Document comment extraction, missing-comment handling, sample alignment, and training comparability. Controlled evidence or narrower claims about this particular unfiltered-comment condition are needed.

Necessary—limit claims about semantic correctness to the available evidence. BLEU, GLEU, ROUGE, and exact match primarily measure reference agreement. They do not establish functional correctness of reconstructed programs or factual completeness of summaries, and no systematic human evaluation addresses the human-perception component of RQ2. Figure 8 even prints an incomplete shift expression in a positive example. Provide semantic validation or describe the findings as improvements in textual reconstruction.

Necessary—clarify the executable method and calibrate the quantitative conclusions. Figure 3 concatenates embeddings, whereas Equations 8 and 10 sum them; modality selection differs between Algorithm 1 and Section 2.4; and gradient handling for the model-dependent targets in Equation 5 is unspecified. Decoder and checkpoint details also need clarification. Single-seed results do not substantiate repeated claims of significant, robust superiority: Table 6 shows lower BLEU than GraphCodeBERT and gains of only 0.53 GLEU and 0.43 exact-match points. Report uncertainty or qualify these claims. Section 5.1 also incorrectly labels relative percentage decreases as point decreases.

Optional—shorten the repeated human-learning analogies, improve figure-label legibility, and strengthen the qualitative embedding analysis with semantic annotations or measurements in the original embedding space. These would improve communication; the recommendation primarily reflects unresolved experimental interpretation and claim support.
